seg_p0035_s0001: were received lukewarmly by the inhabitants; yet among some entirely, and among others less so, they persisted right up to the persecution of Diocletian." So Gildas; and where he speaks of the time toward the close of Tiberius, this must be explained from Eusebius's Chronicle, in which, under either the last or the second-to-last year of Tiberius, it is noted: "When Pilate reported to Tiberius concerning the doctrine of the Christians, Tiberius referred the matter to the senate, that it might be received among the other sacred rites. But when, by a decree of the fathers, it had been resolved that the Christians should be expelled from the city, Tiberius by an edict threatened death to the accusers of the Christians.
seg_p0035_s0002: So Tertullian writes in his Apology."
seg_p0035_s0003: The words of Tertullian are these: "Tiberius, in whose time the Christian name entered the world, when word was brought to him from Syria Palestine that the truth of that divinity had there been revealed, laid it before the senate with the prerogative of his own vote in its favour. The senate, because it had not itself approved it, rejected it.
seg_p0035_s0004: Caesar held to his opinion, threatening danger to the accusers of the Christians." To this Eusebius adds, in book two of the Ecclesiastical History, chapter three, in the translation of Rufinus:
seg_p0035_s0005: "This indeed divine providence at that time so impressed upon Caesar's mind, that, with no obstacle whatever, in the very first beginnings the word of the Gospel might run everywhere on every side. Whence it also came about that suddenly, as though a light were shown from heaven, or a certain ray of the sun bursting forth, the brightness of that heavenly light illumined the whole world: so that the prophecy was fulfilled which had said, Their sound went out into all the earth — namely, of the evangelists and apostles — and their words to the ends of the world. From this, throughout all cities and villages, immense multitudes of people were gathered to the Churches, as grain is gathered to the threshing floors at harvest time." "The congregation of the Christians made its way into every kind of mankind; nor did any nation of the Roman world remain that was left without a share in his worship." Μία ἡ ἐκκλησία, ἣν ἱδρύσαντο οἱ ἅγιοι ἀπόστολοι ἀπὸ περάτων ἕως περάτων ἐν τῷ αἵματι τοῦ Χριστοῦ, οἰκείοις ἱδρῶσι καὶ πόνοις [There is one Church, which the holy apostles founded from end to end in the blood of Christ, by their own sweat and toils].
